BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE GAJENDRA SINGH  ON THE 2 nd OF FEBRUARY, 2026  CRIMINAL APPEAL No. 5148 of 2024  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH  Versus  AJAY  Appearance:
 Shri Rahul Solanki - G.A. for the appellant/State.
 Shri Ankit Bhalavi - Advocate for the respondent.
 ORDER

This criminal appeal is preferred under Section 14A(2) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act r/w Section 439(2) of Cr.P.C., 1973 for recall of order dated 04.01.2023 in CRA No.11124/2022 in the nature of cancellation of bail in connection with Crime No.268/2022 registered at P.S. Barwah,
District Khargone (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 294, 147, 149, 323,
506, 307, 302 and 120-B of IPC and Sections 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s), 3(2)(v-a) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

2. The respondent/accused was extended the benefit of bail with a condition that he shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. Section 439(1)A says that any person accused of an offence and in custody by released on bail, and if the offence is of the nature specified in sub-section (3) of Section 437, may impose any condition which it considers necessary for the purpose mentioned in that sub-section.

For ready reference, Section 437(3) is reproduced below:-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3703 2 CRA-5148-2024 "When a person accused or suspected of the commission of an offence punishable with imprisonment which may extend to seven years or more or of an offence under Chapter VI, Chapter XVI or Chapter XVII of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860) or abetment of, or conspiracy or attempt to commit, any such offence, is released on bail under sub- section (1), [the Court shall impose the conditions,-
(a)that such person shall attend in accordance with the conditions of the bond executed under this Chapter,

entities.text: Chapter VI, Chapter XVI or Chapter XVII
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: 1 b)that such person shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected, and (c)that such person shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence,and may also impose, in the interests of justice, such other conditions as it considers necessary".

4. This application is preferred on the ground that after releasing on bail he committed an offence registered as Crime No.0715/2023 registered at P.S. Barwaha, Khargone for the offence punishable under Sections 354, 354(A)(1)(i), 354(C)(1)(i) and 506 of IPC and Sections 7 and 8 of POCSO Act,
2012 and another crime bearing Crime No.572/2023 registered at P.S. Kasrawad, Khargone for the offence punishable under Section 363, 376, 376(3), 506 r/w 34 of the IPC and Section 3 and 4 of the POCSO Act, 2012.

The Crime No.572/2023 was registered on 30.12.2023 and Crime No.715/2023 was registered on 31.12.2023.
5.

The respondent/accused opposed the application by filing reply through Document No.10208/2025 and has submitted that the present appeal filed by the appellant-State for cancellation of bail is devoid of merit, not maintainable in the eyes of law, and liable to be dismissed referring to the case of State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Rashid Khan @ Arif Khan, Supreme 2024 (MP)
744 in which it is held that bail cannot be cancelled merely on ground of registration of another offence subsequently.

entities.text:
State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Rashid Khan @ Arif Khan, Supreme 2024 (MP)
744
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paragraph of the said judgment is mentioned herein below:-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3703 3 CRA-5148-2024 5.

In view of the aforesaid, it is clear that cancellation of bail and the power of cancelling bail cannot be exercised by the Court in a mechanical manner; if nature of offence which has been committed subsequent to the offence in which bail has been granted, is same, then the Court should consider the aspect as to whether subsequent offence is otherwise prejudicial of the smooth trial of the case in which bail has been granted or it otherwise attempts to evade the due course of justice or abuse of the concession granted to the accused in any manner.
6.

In this case having been released on bail vide order dated 04.01.2023 in a heinous offence, the present appellant jeopardised the safety of children and subsequently committed another heinous offence under the provisions of the POCSO Act, 2012.
Such subsequent conduct constitutes a grave intervening circumstance, thereby satisfying the settled parameters for cancellation of bail.
In view of the above, the present criminal appeal is allowed.
Consequently, the order granting bail dated 04.01.2023 is set aside.
The bail bonds furnished by the appellant stand cancelled and the sureties are hereby discharged.
7. The trial Court is directed to take the respondent/accused in custody.
